scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents note
scopecontent.p: The Rockefeller Foundation fellowship recorder cards provide introductory access and basic summary information for each fellow and fellowship including but not limited to: name, country of origin, division authorizing the award, subject and discipline of fellowship. Medical sciences, nursing, agriculture (plants and animals), and public health comprise most of the disciplines involved but there are a few others. The recorder cards also document awards given by the General Education Board and the boards established by the Rockefeller Foundation including the International Education Board and China Medical Board. Information on the recorder cards was collected from the RF RG 10.1 Fellowship Files by RF administrative staff, and they are best used in conjunction with these files. Please note that not every fellow who has a file will necessarily have a recorder card and all recorder cards do not necessarily have corresponding files. Please look at both indices to verify if a fellow has both a file and a recorder card.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: Digitized copies of the Rockefeller Foundation Fellowship Recorder Cards have been used by a research team based in Geneva and Lausanne (Switzerland) to develop an online searchable database titled "Rockefeller Fellows: History of Individual Mobility Awards at Rockefeller-endowed Organizations, 1914-1970". The Rockefeller Fellows database is hosted on the Heurist platform, which enabled the research team to work with the complete dataset based on the original cards, to add new fields and values not present in the cards but based on their historical research, and to make the dataset publicly available in accordance with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

The Rockefeller Archive Center's collaboration with the Swiss research team on this project was limited to providing digitized copies of the original cards and supporting their historical research in the RAC's reading rooms. The Rockefeller Archive Center does not endorse any historical conclusions drawn by the research team based on the cards or any new fields, values, or information added by the research team to the dataset that were not present in the original cards.
